LanguageData.chupakobra6_2969748433_BiomeVariant_BMT_: Water and weathering have carved out branching networks of caverns beneath the sand and stone of the desert. With the searing hot sun unable to reach, the subterranean nature of this environment lends itself to cooler living for anything within.

Sitting within the sometimes kilometers thick ice of permanently frozen regions, these hollows have never seen warmth. Nearly every surface is made of solid ice, so dense and cold that they are impervious to heat, with any warmth quickly drawn away. Little life can survive here, but what does is unsurprisingly quite hardy.
A molten landscape unfolds on the surface, marked by liquid lava and active calderas. The dormant lava tubes leading to the depths unveil a hidden subterranean world.

A shallow system of caves close to or connecting to the surface world. This proximity to the surface has led to a fascinating mix of life from both the surface and the UnderRim. While these caverns sometimes connect safely via tunnels, they are occasionally only accessible via sinkhole or crevasse.
